difficultyReason: Two straightforward facts with one direct logical consequence. The stimulus states all tulips are perennials, and this particular flower is a tulip. The correct answer simply applies the categorical rule to the specific case.
stimulus: All tulips are perennials. The flower that bloomed in the garden last spring is a tulip.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Some perennials bloom in the spring.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The flower that bloomed in the garden last spring is a perennial.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All flowers that bloom in the spring are tulips.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The flower that bloomed in the garden last spring will bloom again next year.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tulips are the most common perennial found in gardens.

explanations.correct: If all tulips are perennials, and the flower in the garden is a tulip, then it must be a perennial. This is a direct application of a universal categorical statement to a specific member.
explanations.A: While this could be true, it is not entailed by the stimulus. We know one tulip bloomed in spring, but this does not entail that some perennials do.
explanations.C: This reverses the logic. The stimulus says all tulips are perennials, not all spring bloomers are tulips.
explanations.D: Perennials return annually, but the stimulus gives no information about whether this particular flower will bloom again.
explanations.E: The stimulus contains no information about the frequency or commonality of tulips.

difficultyReason: Simple two-fact stimulus with conditional logic. If all members of the board are appointed by the mayor, and Chen is a board member, then Chen must be appointed by the mayor. One-step modus ponens.
stimulus: Everyone who serves on the city planning board is appointed by the mayor. Chen serves on the city planning board.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mayor appoints everyone who works for the city.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chen was appointed by the mayor.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All of the mayor's appointees serve on the city planning board.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mayor's appointment decisions are always made fairly.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No one except the mayor can appoint board members.

explanations.correct: The first statement is a universal conditional: all board members are mayoral appointees. Chen is a board member. Therefore, Chen must be a mayoral appointee.
explanations.A: The stimulus says only that board members are appointed by the mayor, not that the mayor appoints all city workers.
explanations.C: This inverts the conditional. The stimulus does not say that all appointees serve on the board.
explanations.D: The stimulus makes no claim about the fairness or quality of the mayor's decisions.
explanations.E: The stimulus does not exclude other entities from appointing board members; it only states that board members are appointed by the mayor.

difficultyReason: Three simple facts combined to yield one necessary conclusion. Combining sets: all aspirin is analgesic, all analgesics are pain relievers, therefore all aspirin are pain relievers. Transitive chain with one link, straightforward.
stimulus: All aspirin is analgesic medication. All analgesic medication relieves pain. Aspirin was developed in the late nineteenth century.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pain relief was unknown before aspirin was developed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All medication that relieves pain is analgesic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aspirin relieves pain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aspirin is the most widely used pain reliever.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All analgesic medication was developed in the nineteenth century.

explanations.correct: Since all aspirin is analgesic, and all analgesics relieve pain, aspirin must relieve pain. This is a simple transitive chain: aspirin → analgesic → pain relief.
explanations.A: The stimulus says aspirin was developed in the late nineteenth century, not that pain relief did not exist before.
explanations.B: The stimulus tells us analgesics relieve pain, not that all pain relievers are analgesics.
explanations.D: The stimulus contains no comparative claims about the prevalence of aspirin.
explanations.E: The stimulus only establishes that aspirin was developed in the nineteenth century, not all analgesics.

difficultyReason: Straightforward negation and contrapositive. If violating the code results in disciplinary action, and Ms. Wong was not disciplined, then she did not violate the code. Contrapositive of a simple conditional.
stimulus: All employees who violate the employee conduct code are subject to disciplinary action. Ms. Wong was not subject to disciplinary action.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ms. Wong is an exemplary employee.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some employees who do not violate the conduct code are not disciplined.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ms. Wong did not violate the employee conduct code.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Everyone who is not disciplined did not violate the conduct code.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The employee conduct code is strictly enforced.

explanations.correct: By contrapositive: if all violators are disciplined, then anyone not disciplined did not violate. Ms. Wong was not disciplined, so she did not violate the code.
explanations.A: The stimulus provides no information about the overall quality of Ms. Wong's performance.
explanations.B: This may be true, but it is not entailed by the stimulus. We only know about one undisciplined employee.
explanations.D: This overgeneralizes. While Ms. Wong is not disciplined and did not violate, we cannot infer that all non-disciplined people did not violate (there may be gaps in enforcement).
explanations.E: The stimulus provides no information about enforcement rigor.

difficultyReason: Two facts with a simple logical intersection. If only English majors can take the advanced seminar, and Marcus is enrolled in it, then Marcus must be an English major. Direct application of a rule to a specific case.
stimulus: Only English majors are permitted to enroll in the advanced literature seminar. Marcus is enrolled in the advanced literature seminar.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Marcus will graduate with an English degree.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All English majors are enrolled in the advanced literature seminar.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Marcus is an English major.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The advanced literature seminar is taught by the English department.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No student with a double major can enroll in the advanced literature seminar.

explanations.correct: Only English majors can take the seminar. Marcus is in the seminar. Therefore, Marcus must be an English major.
explanations.A: Enrollment in one advanced seminar does not guarantee graduation with that major.
explanations.B: The stimulus says only English majors can enroll, not that all English majors do enroll.
explanations.D: The stimulus provides no information about which department teaches the course.
explanations.E: The stimulus places no restriction on double majors.

difficultyReason: Two separate negative facts with no logical bridge between them. While each fact is true, neither entails anything about the other. One-step recognition that the stimulus does not support the conclusion.
stimulus: No mammals are reptiles. No birds are reptiles.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All birds are mammals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No mammals are birds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some animals that are not reptiles are either mammals or birds.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mammals and birds belong to the same biological family.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reptiles exist in nature.

explanations.correct: We know that mammals are not reptiles and birds are not reptiles. This means there exist animals (both mammals and birds) that are not reptiles. Choice C simply states this necessary conclusion in hedged language.
explanations.A: The stimulus does not connect birds and mammals; knowing they are both non-reptiles does not make all birds mammals.
explanations.B: Mammals and birds are not reptiles, but that does not preclude their overlap.
explanations.D: The stimulus provides no information about biological classification beyond reptile status.
explanations.E: The stimulus only makes claims about which animals are not reptiles; it does not entail that reptiles exist.

difficultyReason: Simple categorical fact: all members of a defined group share a property. If all board members have voting rights, and Rodriguez is a board member, then Rodriguez has voting rights. One-step modus ponens.
stimulus: All members of the corporate board have voting rights in shareholder meetings. Rodriguez is a member of the corporate board.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rodriguez is a shareholder.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rodriguez has voting rights in shareholder meetings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Shareholders are members of the corporate board.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All shareholders have voting rights.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rodriguez's voting rights are greater than those of other board members.

explanations.correct: All board members have voting rights. Rodriguez is a board member. Therefore, Rodriguez must have voting rights.
explanations.A: The stimulus says board members have voting rights; it does not equate board members with shareholders.
explanations.C: This reverses the relationship. Board members have voting rights in shareholder meetings, but the stimulus does not make them shareholders.
explanations.D: The stimulus only addresses board members, not all shareholders.
explanations.E: The stimulus provides no comparative information about voting power among board members.

difficultyReason: Three facts: a universal rule, a specific instance, and a temporal fact. Combining the rule with the instance yields the necessary inference. The temporal fact is incidental noise.
stimulus: All marine vessels registered in this port must comply with the new safety standards. The ferry that operates between the two islands is registered in this port. The safety standards were enacted last year.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The ferry began operating after the safety standards were enacted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ferry must comply with the new safety standards.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All ferries must comply with the new safety standards.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The safety standards have improved ferry transportation between the islands.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No vessel that was not registered in this port needs to comply with the standards.

explanations.correct: All vessels registered in the port must comply. The ferry is registered in the port. Therefore, the ferry must comply with the new safety standards.
explanations.A: The stimulus only says when the standards were enacted, not when the ferry began operating.
explanations.C: Only vessels registered in this particular port must comply; the stimulus does not address all ferries generally.
explanations.D: The stimulus provides no information about the efficacy or impact of the standards.
explanations.E: The stimulus addresses only vessels in this port; it does not restrict vessels outside the port.

difficultyReason: Two straightforward facts: all members of a defined linguistic group use a certain feature, and a specific person is a member. Therefore, that person must use the feature. One-step categorical inference.
stimulus: All speakers of the Mandarin dialect in this region use a distinctive tone pattern. Professor Liu is a speaker of the Mandarin dialect in this region.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anyone who uses a distinctive tone pattern speaks the Mandarin dialect.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Professor Liu uses a distinctive tone pattern.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Mandarin dialect is the most common dialect in the region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All tone patterns are distinctive.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Professor Liu has lived in the region her entire life.

explanations.correct: All speakers of the regional Mandarin dialect use this tone pattern. Professor Liu speaks it. Therefore, Professor Liu must use the tone pattern.
explanations.A: The stimulus says all Mandarin speakers use the pattern, not that only Mandarin speakers use it.
explanations.C: The stimulus provides no information about the prevalence or commonality of the dialect.
explanations.D: The stimulus discusses only the tone pattern used by Mandarin speakers in the region.
explanations.E: The stimulus provides no biographical information about Professor Liu.

difficultyReason: Three facts: a universal principle, a specific case, and a time reference. Applying the principle to the case yields one necessary inference. The time reference provides context but does not prevent the inference.
stimulus: Every artwork displayed in the museum's permanent collection has been authenticated by the chief curator. The portrait in the East Wing is displayed in the museum's permanent collection. The portrait was donated to the museum five years ago.
questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The portrait was authenticated by the chief curator.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The chief curator examined the portrait five years ago.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All donated artworks are displayed in the permanent collection.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The portrait is more valuable than other artworks in the East Wing.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The chief curator authenticates every artwork the museum acquires.

explanations.correct: Every artwork in the permanent collection has been authenticated by the chief curator. The portrait is in the permanent collection. Therefore, the portrait must have been authenticated by the chief curator.
explanations.B: The portrait was donated five years ago, but we do not know when it was authenticated—it could have been before or after.
explanations.C: The stimulus tells us the portrait is displayed and was donated, but this does not entail that all donations are displayed.
explanations.D: The stimulus provides no comparative value information.
explanations.E: The stimulus addresses artworks in the permanent collection, not all acquisitions.
